purpose: Behavioral prompts and criteria; not a claim that every scenario has been executed.

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to explain a Bell pair in an interactive machine. Let me zoom, pan, separate its layers and reassemble them, then solve a small challenge.
checks: Quantum probabilities and relative phase derive from one model
Local Bloch views do not claim to display the full entangled state
Manual camera input interrupts choreography
Repeated reassembly returns to the rest pose
The challenge checks a genuine objective and supports restart

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to explain how a small causal transformer turns tokens into a next-token distribution. Separate one attention block and let me inspect its values.
checks: Computes an explicit small Q/K/V example and causal mask
Shows softmax weights and residual flow consistently
Labels toy weights and tokenization assumptions
Does not invent a universal architecture

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to make a glowing hydrogen orbital I can rotate, slice, and zoom into, with a guided explanation.
checks: Uses orbital probability rather than unlabelled planetary orbits
Explains density, scale distortion and any exaggerated nucleus
Preserves readable labels under zoom
Reduced motion preserves inspection

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to explain a black hole. Fly from an overview to the photon ring, then give me free pan and zoom.
checks: Separates horizon, shadow, disk and lensing
Sources the physical model and names approximations
Does not call a decorative vortex exact general relativity
Extreme zoom preserves clipping and orientation

evaluations.prompt: Use this diagram claiming extra dimensions are definitely relational degrees of freedom as inspiration for a beautiful explainer.
checks: Treats the image as art direction, not scientific evidence
Labels speculative interpretations
Seeks a primary source for a specific proposed theory

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to make one static SVG of an exploded camera lens for a light-background article. No web app.
checks: Honors static SVG output
Does not add a timeline, game or deployment
Preserves optical ordering and verifies specifications

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster for an assembly that survives interrupted separation, backward scrubbing, repeated reassembly and a narrow phone viewport.
checks: Stores immutable rest transforms and stable part IDs
Samples absolute poses from one progress value
Tests intermediate states and backward seeks
Responsive framing does not fight navigation

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to start a new interactive explainer in an empty temporary directory, keeping the skill checkout untouched.
checks: Uses skill-relative helper paths
Generated code runs without importing the installed skill directory
Reports actual build and browser checks
Leaves unrelated files and projects unchanged

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to explain a mounting plate being built in CAD, like smlibpy.classcad.ch. Keep it sober, with code linked to each operation.
checks: Uses restrained orthographic engineering style without decorative glow
Executes actual CAD operations or labels geometry schematic
Keeps code, measured values, captions, and stage geometry synchronized
Replays complete snapshots when scrubbing backward
Distinguishes exact STEP from unitless tessellated STL and verifies exports

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster for a sober two-joint robot arm explanation. Show local axes and an exploded inspection view. No game.
checks: Uses a kinematic parent hierarchy and explicit units
Keeps joint origins, axes, and limits authoritative
Separates inspection offsets from operational joint transforms
Does not add gameplay or send hardware commands
Checks known poses and exact reassembly

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to explain an FDM printer layer by layer, with perimeters, infill and travel.
checks: Distinguishes model, slices, and toolpath data
Labels schematic paths unless a real slicer supplies them
Synchronizes nozzle, visible deposition, and layer count
Does not fill travel moves or imply a decorative path is ready G-code
Uses quiet camera and accurate layer/nozzle scale

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to explain a protein–ligand interface with experimental structure coordinates. Let me inspect chains, residues, representations and measured contacts, and scrub the explanation.
checks: Records structure ID, assembly/model, method, provenance, coordinate units and missing-data choices
Preserves atom and residue identities across rendering and picking
Reports distances from original coordinates, with contact cutoffs distinguished from chemical bonds
Does not describe a static structure or camera animation as molecular dynamics
Manual navigation interrupts camera motion and reduced motion preserves inspection

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to explain Taster in an interactive editorial diagram inspired by Diagram Design and Archify, using Taster’s existing identity. Include a portable SVG.
checks: Topology and labeled edge semantics express the actual workflow
Uses the existing logo, local typefaces and semantic brand colors
Selection and keyboard inspection reveal meaningful content
Export embeds needed assets and retains an accessible title and description
Checks full and focused routes for clipping and label collisions at desktop and narrow sizes

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to produce a branded short video explaining Taster with Hyperframes, editable HTML and a rendered MP4.
checks: Provides an actual deterministic Hyperframes-compatible composition and pinned render instructions
Waits for required local assets before frame capture
Repeated and reverse seeking to a timestamp reproduce the same scene
Exports and inspects encoded frames, dimensions, frame rate and duration
Does not call a browser preview an encoded video or claim an unexecuted render succeeded

evaluations.prompt: Use $taster to visualize my molecular dynamics trajectory with receptor, membrane and solvent. Let me scrub time and inspect a selected lipid.
checks: Validates topology-to-frame atom mapping and physical time units
Handles periodic boundaries and alignment explicitly without fabricating missing frames
Bounds geometry cost and preserves selected molecule identity
Labels any interpolated frames and distinguishes structural metrics from decorative motion
Reports unsupported file formats or absent trajectory data rather than substituting a simulated result
